These are animations written against `Canvas.timeline()`: a script reads as a
storyboard of clips, and the timeline compiles them into ordinary keyframes on
the camera rig, node inputs, entity properties and annotations. There is one
storyboard for each example in
[ProteinMotion's `examples/`](https://github.com/pdpppd/proteinmotion/tree/main/examples),
so the two can be compared scene for scene. Each page shows the render and the
script that made it; the scripts live in `docs/examples/timeline/scripts/` and
are not run when the documentation is built.

::: {.callout-note}
This is a proof of concept of the timeline API. Several ProteinMotion effects
need nodes that Molecular Nodes does not have yet; each page says where its
storyboard stops short, and the list at the bottom collects them.
:::

::: {#storyboards}
:::

## Running a storyboard

Every script is stand-alone and writes an MP4, a few still frames and a
contact sheet into the directory it is given:

```bash
uv run python docs/examples/timeline/scripts/quickstart.py out_dir
MN_EXAMPLES_QUICK=1 uv run python docs/examples/timeline/scripts/quickstart.py out_dir   # small and fast
MN_EXAMPLES_ENGINE=CYCLES uv run python docs/examples/timeline/scripts/quickstart.py out_dir   # no GPU
```

Structures are fetched into the Molecular Nodes download cache on first use.
`_common.py` holds the shared setup and the few helpers the scripts need:
painting a selection's colour, a transparent context material, cutting between
style nodes, titles and callouts, spinning an object about its centre.

## What maps onto what

| ProteinMotion | Molecular Nodes |
| --- | --- |
| `self.play(..., run_time=)`, `self.wait()` | `t.play(..., run_time=)`, `t.wait()` |
| `camera.animate.orbit(theta=)`, `Rotate(protein, a)` | `canvas.camera.orbit(deg)`, `spin(mol, deg)` |
| `self.focus(region)`, `Focus(camera, region)` | `canvas.camera.look_at(view, margin=)` |
| `camera.set_focus(...)`, `FocusPull(camera, region, fstop=)` | `canvas.camera.focus(view, fstop=)` |
| `camera.zoom(f)` | `canvas.camera.zoom(lens)` |
| `Representation(p, name)` | `show_only(t, styles, [style])`: a cut, keyed on the style's `Selection` input |
| `region.set_color(c)`, `Colorize(region, c)` | `paint(mol, selection, c)` into the `Color` attribute (static) |
| `SetOpacity(region, x)` | a second style on the region with `mn.material.Transparent`, its `transparency` socket tweened |
| `ColorByProperty(p, values)` | `color=lambda: mg.ColorAttributeMap(name=, min=, max=)` |
| `PlayTrajectory(p, start=, end=)` | `mol.play(start, end)` |
| `Text(...)`, `region.callout(...)` | `title(mol, ...)` (2D label), `callout(mol, selection, ...)` (3D label at the selection's centre with a pointer) |
| `Distance(a, b)` | `mol.annotations.add_com_distance(...)` |
| `Trajectory.aligned(indices=)` | `align_frames(mol, selection)` (MDAnalysis `AlignTraj`, in memory) |
| `DensityMap.from_file`, `isosurface`, `slice` | `Grids.load(..., style="density_iso_surface")`, `threshold` and `slice_center` inputs |

## Not there yet

- **Opacity per atom** (`FadeIn`/`FadeOut`, `SetOpacity` with `residue_delay`): needs a `Set Opacity` node. The `Default` material already reads the `Color` attribute's alpha, so a static opacity can be painted.
- **Staggered per-residue changes** (`residue_delay=` on colour, opacity, morphs): needs the `Animate Stagger` node.
- **Morphs and deformations** (`Morph`, `BackboneMorph`, `Deform`, `ContactMatch`): need `Morph To Attribute`. The morph storyboards cut between the two structures.
- **3D highlights** (`region.highlight(style="sphere" | "box" | "atoms")`): a `Style Highlight` node. The regions are painted instead.
- **Hydrogen bonds and electrostatics** (`HydrogenBonds`, `Electrostatics`): analysis nodes plus a dashed-bond style. One pair is drawn with a distance annotation where it matters.
- **Write-on text** (`Write`, `Unwrite`): a `progress` property on text annotations. Labels are cut in and out.
- **Plots and legends** (`ContactMap`, `TimeSeriesPlot`, `SequenceTrack`, `ColorLegend`): plot annotations.
- **Cross-fading representations**: needs opacity; representation changes are cuts.
- **Depth cue**: no shortcut for a mist pass.
- ProteinMotion's `contact_report.py` has no counterpart: it is a matplotlib report on its own contact-matching output, not a scene.

The design notes for the timeline are in `docs/dev/canvas-timeline.md`, and the
survey these storyboards follow from is `docs/dev/protein-motion-comparison.md`.
